content: I'm thinking about uploading our revised paper onto arXiv. What edits should we me make to the version submitted to the ITP/unabridged version before submitting it online?

Sure, we can upload a new version to arXiv.

It makes more sense to me to extend the arXiv version with the new sections/paragraphs from the ITP version, rather than to expand and polish the ITP paper. What do yall think?
Since nobody else is responding, I suppose I'll just go ahead and do this. I'll let you know when I'm finished.

main.pdf
I think we are ready to submit the preprint version of our paper onto arXiv. What do you all think?
A message was moved here from #Seymour > Pictures for the paper by Martin Dvořák.
Does anyone here have perms to upload the finished revision of the paper to arXiv? @Martin Dvořák has been inactive for a while now.
Sorry for the long delay. I moved to Czechia and I was without internet at home until today.
You write "Independent" under your name. Should we write the same under @Alex Nelson (iirc, he doesn't have any affiliation, but let me know if things changed)?
Sure, we can do that.
main.pdf
Should people without affiliation have location written there?
I think it's fine to.
OK, let's wait for what @Alex Nelson says.

Regarding writing locations for people (like me) who are "independent" is fine...I have no strong opinion one way or the other. If you want to add a location for me, I usually use "Los Angeles, California" for my location.
Since he doesn't have a preference, I think we should just upload it as it is @Martin Dvořák.
Well, I have a preference for uniformity. If you want to keep your location there, can you add his location as well please?

main.pdf
Here's the draft with @Alex Nelson's location.
Thanks! So I'll upload the pdf as revision to arXiv, ok?
Sorry, I've been extremely busy today. I hope I will upload it tomorrow.

main.pdf appears to have been produced by TeX

This file has been rejected as part your submission because it appears to be pdf generated from TeX/LaTeX source. For the reasons outlined at in the Why TeX FAQ we insist on submission of the TeX source rather than the processed version.

Our software includes an automatic TeX processing script that will produce PDF, PostScript and dvi from your TeX source. If our determination that your submission is TeX produced is incorrect, you should send e-mail with your submission number to arXiv administrators.

It seems that the exemption we got was only for the first submission, which I uploaded as a PDF even tho it was generated from TeX. Can you please give me a .zip file with all the source files?
Sure. As a side note, we unfortunately got rejected from ITP :(. You probably received an email as well – let me know what you think of their feedback.
Seymour_Paper (20) 2.zip

Cameron Rampell said:

You probably received an email as well – let me know what you think of their feedback.

Yeah. Sad.

The most shocking part of the reviews is that they cricize us for using undefined notions in Introduction. Throughout my entire Ph.D., I was taught to only mention things in the Introduction and define them later. Does the ITP community expect something else?

As for the metaänalysis of the achievement and hurdles, as I already said several times, somebody else will have to write it. Metaänalysis was not on my radar when working on the project. My one and only goal was to make the proof sorry-free (and maintain good code hygiene throughout the project and especially for the release version), not to "learn" about the process of formalization!
Could I ask for a small clarification: what is meant by "meta-analysis" in this situation? (I'm coming from a physics background, where meta-analysis means something probably completely different...)

My 2 cents as an outsider (and not an expert on the mathematics): what I would have expected, and hardly find at all in the draft above,
is a discussion of the formalisation design trade-offs: which design choices did you have to make, why did you decide as you did, what did you learn about the right design in the process? (Playing devil's advocate, at this point "I formalised X" alone is not that interesting --- write about what it taught you in the process, be it the mathematics, the process, the design decisions, etc.)

If you write about the formalisation process, you do so very implicitly. You have a section "suggestions for mathlib"... which contains interesting pieces (such as custom notation, writing your own delaborators, etc. --- custom metaprogramming is not common, you're selling your own work short)!

Getting into subjective territory, it might be helpful to use more top-level sections (such as related work (put earlier?), background, the mathematical argument, design trade-offs, challenges faced, mathlib suggestions... right now, your paper looks like "only the math", and this shows).
Is my first paragraph what you mean by "meta-analysis"?

The mathematical argument is too long for inclusion in the formalization paper. The mathematical argument is a subject of the blueprint.

That said, I still don't know much about what to actually write in our paper. Given that all informal content is in the blueprint and all formal content is in the code, what remains to be discussed in the paper?

Michael Rothgang said:

Is my first paragraph what you mean by "meta-analysis"?

I'm not sure, the anonymous reviewers wrote (in their "Meta-review" section of comments): "However, they agree that there are issues with the presentation: assuming too much knowledge of matroid theory, Lean 4, and not enough meta-analysis of the formalisation's goals, achievements, and hurdles." (emphasis added)

Martin Dvořák said:

That said, I still don't know much about what to actually write in our paper. Given that all informal content is in the blueprint and all formal content is in the code, what remains to be discussed in the paper?

I think the first paragraph of Michael's answer is exactly about this - it's neither directly about the informal or the formal content, nor about the mathematical argument

I don't think I have what it takes to write a short and understandable summary of our design decisions.

One decision decision we discuss in an older version of the paper is Matrix.toMatrixDropUnionDrop vs Matrix.toMatrixDropUnionDropInternal but it was cut out for being too long (which is fair because it took me nearly three pages to get across my point).
